GLOSSARY

AF (ALTERNATIVE FREQUENCY):

Radio function which makes it possible, whilst receiving an RDS programme broadcast by several transmitters on different frequencies, to automatically switch to the frequency with the best reception.

BALANCE

Radio function which makes it possible to adjust the sound distribution between the left and right side speakers.

BASS

Radio function which makes it possible to adjust the acoustics (LOW TONES)

EON

Radio device function which makes it possible to receive information on traffic conditions from radio channels not currently tuned into, temporarily interrupting the station being listened to.

FADER

Radio function which makes it possible to adjust the distribution of the sound between the speakers

FM

Long wave radio transmission frequency between 8705 and 108 MHz.

GPS (GLOBAL POSITIONING SISTEM)

Satellite location system, whose purpose is to provide any user the possibility of deciding his position on the earth's surface.

GSM

Communication standard for mobile equipment (GSM= Global System for Mobile Communcation) currently used in about 90 countries, enjoying optimum coverage.

LOUDNESS

Radio function which makes it possible to improve the sound by increasing the low tones.

LW

Long wave radio transmission frequency between 153 and 279 kHz.

MW

Long wave radio transmission frequency between 531 and 1602 kHz.

POI (Point of interest)

Consists of typing in a sequence of information in order to select a particular point of interest (in relation to which information can be obtained)

Radio function which makes it possible, with the RADIO mode activated, to select the type of programme, e.g. NEWS (news and current affairs), AFFAIRS (politics and events), etc. for the radio stations which provide this type of information.

Specifications

Introduction

The Telematic Info Node (CONNECT) is an electronic device connected to the B-CAN network which incorporates the radio, music CD player, Navigator and the GSM car 'phone with Voice Recognition module. The TIN is mounted at the centre of the dashboard and occupies 2 DIN slots (1 DIN slot corresponds to the standard dimensions of a car radio).

Cars fitted with CONNECT also have an instructions document for use of the radio/CD, car 'phone and Navigator

The external components which complete the CONNECT functions are:

  • Loudspeakers, in the two versions HIGH level and HI FI level (see subgroup 5570T)
  • The radio aerial with radio, telephone and satellite navigator functions
  • A CD CHANGER with 10-disc loader supplied as OPT (see subgroup 5570T)

Introduction

Switching the system on/off and stand-by

The system can assume one of the following conditions:

  • off, with all the functions disabled;
  • normal status, with all the functions activated or able to be activated;
  • stand-by, with the functions partly activated and the screen dark

System activation

The system is activated automatically when the ignition is turned ON and it assumes the status activated before it was switched off last time (normal or stand-by).

When the ignition key is turned OFF or removed, the system comes on by pressing the left knob (T16) or the SOS button (T22) for a 'Service Call' (the PIN number must be entered in order to use the telephone).

Turning the system off

The system switches off automatically when the ignition key is turned to the OFF position. The conditions and functions activated before the system is switched off are memorized and will be restored the next time it is switched on.

The switching off is delayed if a phonecall or an emergency call is in progress or if there is a change of language for the voice instructions by about 20 minutes after the call has ended or at the end of the function.

If the system has been switched on using the knob (T16) or the button (T22) with the ignition key in the OFF position or extracted, it is switched off by pressing the knob (T16) again or it switches off automatically about 20 minutes later to preserve the battery.

Stand-by (dark)

Whilst the system is operating with the ignition key inserted, it can be placed in the stand-by mode by pressing the MAIN button (T17) at length. This operating condition (Dark) corresponds to a dark screen with the volume off, but the system continues to work invisibly and therefore the telephone is ready to receive calls.

If the limit of an activated function is exceeded in the stand-by mode, a warning is displayed.

To return to normal operating conditions, press the MAIN button (T17) or the emergency call button (T22) briefly (the PIN number must be entered in order to use the phone).

Hold the NAV key down to deactivate the navigation system voice instructions (T20). The volume gradually decreases (Soft Mute function) and the message 'NAV MUTE' appears on the display.

Give the NAV key (T20) a long press to deactivate the NAV MUTE function: the volume will gradually increase (Soft Mute function) to the previous setting.

With the NAV MUTE function active, all other navigation system functions can be used and the MUTE function will be ignored if traffic information is received with the TA function active or an emergency alarm is received.

When the MUTE function (audio system) or NAV MUTE (navigation system) is turned on or off, the volume falls or rises gradually (Soft Mute function). The Soft Mute function is activated when one of the six preselection keys numbered 1 to 6 , key (T13) or key (T15) is pressed to tune the radio stations.

Anti-theft protection

The CONNECT system has an anti-theft protection system based on the exchange of information with the electronic control unit (Body Computer) which prevents it from being used on another vehicle even if it is equipped with a Body Computer. The protection system means that the telematic system cannot be used once it has been extracted from the dashboard and stolen.

This 'recognition' procedure is carried out each time the engine is started.

This system guarantees maximum security and prevents the secret code having to be entered each time after the radio supply is disconnected (for example when the battery is disconnected). Each time it is reconnected an automatic test procedure is conducted; if the result of the test is positive, the system starts to work, whilst if the codes compared are not the same, the display shows a message on the display which asks the user to enter the 4 digit secret code

Entering the secret code

The four digit secret code, represented by black asterisks, should be entered using the telephone keypad and confirmed by pressing the knob (R2). The figures entered are shown by red asterisks which replace the black ones.

If one of the code digits needs correcting, press the ESC button (T24) briefly to cancel it, then enter the correct digit. Pressing the ESC button (T24) for longer cancels the entire secret code entered.

After entering and confirming the secret code, a message appears on the display advising the user that the recognition procedure is in progress. If the outcome of the test is positive, the system starts to work normally, whilst if it is not, the screen for entering the code appears again. The system will not work until the correct code has been entered.

The secret code has to be entered for the CONNECT to work after it has been connected to the vehicle's electrical system for the first time or to a different Body Computer from the original one or after a replacement of the system.

Personal data

If the system fails, it cannot be repaired. Instead the full system must be replaced and this entails the loss of any personal data in the memory.

Thermal protection

This complex strategy makes use of several sensors. The following functions are disabled/enabled according to passenger compartment interior temperature:

  • up to 75ºC the system works normally,
  • from 75ºC to 85ºC, the volume is limited, the CD player (audio and maps) is disabled and the phone works normally,
  • at 85ºC the phone is disabled,
  • at 90ºC the system is completely disabled.

The user must wait for passenger compartment temperature to drop below the limit to resume the interrupted function; this condition is signalled by the message on the display disappearing followed by the function being reactivated.

Protection against overheating

The telematic system components come with an overheating protection function that cuts off operation when the relevant module temperature exceeds a set limit.

In this case, the function activated by the module that has reached the temperature limit is deactivated and a message for the user appears on the display.

The user must wait for the module temperature to drop below the limit to resume the interrupted function; this condition is signalled by the message on the display disappearing followed by the function being reactivated.

Conversely, to exit from the message screen immediately and activate a different function, press the ESC key (T24).

The Key On signal is in fact a direct signal to TIN.

General information

1 Screen display active 2 Screen layout display 2 Display of pictogram information

The navigation system in the CONNECT makes it possible to reach a pre-established destination by means of visual instructions (pictograms/maps) and acoustic instructions. The navigation system is fast, convenient, safe and - above all - very flexible to use because it allows you to call up programmed destinations or reference points such as hotels, places of historical interest, public organisations, fuel stations or Alfa Romeo dealers.

The position of the vehicle is determined by means of the GPS (Global Positioning System) on board the vehicle. The GPS system is equipped with an aerial and a receiver module integrated in the telematic system. The system dynamically processes the satellite signals, the signals coming from the left and right milometers, the reversing signal and the information from the gyroscope incorporated in the navigation calculator, integrating them with the current position of the vehicle to produce an 'estimated vehicle point'.

This estimated position tends to differ from the current position as a result of sensor imprecision. To correct this error, every 30 metres an algorithm is activated, called Map Matching, which correlates the journey made by the car with the road network present in the map data base.

The signals coming from the left and right milometers make it possible to determine the movement of the vehicle and whether it has turned off (identified by the difference travelled between the left and right wheels), whilst the reversing sensor identifies the direction of travel.

The Alfa Romeo navigation system helps the driver while driving and advises on the best route to the set destination by means of voice and graphic information.

The suggestions given by the navigation system do not release the driver from full responsability for manoeuvres carried out in traffic while driving the car and for respecting the highway code and other traffic regulations. The responsibility for road safety is always expected from the driver of the vehicle.

GPS reception is difficult under trees, between high buildings, in multi-storey car parks, in tunnels and anywhere where the satellite aerial reception could be obstructed.

If the battery has been disconnected fro the car, the GPS system takes about 15 minutes to become activated.

The GPS navigation system takes a few minutes to pinpoint the new car position after it has been turned off and the car driven without the system active (e.g. on a pick-up truck).

If there is no satellite information, the on board system uses information from the ABS sensors for an analysis of the data.

The GPS satellite aerial should not be covered by metal or damp objects.

This car's instantaneous position is identified in the navigation CD-ROM and shown on the display together with the topographical features of the area memorized on the CD. Access to the data on the CD-ROM requires a brief wait whilst the maps are displayed.

The system constantly compares the information coming from the wheel sensor, the GPS aerial and the gyroscope in order to automatically compensate for variations in temperature, pressure or any other eventuality which could affect the position reading in any way.

The precise autoadjustment of the navigation system requires 50/100 km to be covered after first activation and when the tyres are changed.

If the wheel grip conditions are poor (for example slipping on ice), the system will temporarily give an incorrect position reading.

During the autoadjustment the position reading is incomplete.

The navigation system is completely managed by the telecoms system therefore the only operations which may be necessary are replacing the CD-ROM with one with a map for another area or with an updated map.

Internal functions (localisation)

The GPS measurements used inside the CONNECT nagivation system are:

1 - Estimated position of the vehicle expressed as Latitude / Longitude

Latitude/Longitude values refer to the satellite and are expressed as radiants and Height in metres. The Latitude indicates the reference parallel.

Parallel zero is the equator. Car position is therefore defined as the meridian arc between the point of the car and the reference parallel.

It is essential to indicate whether the latitude is North or South, i.e. it is necessary to specify the hemisphere within which the car is located: North or South, the maximum value is 90°.

The longitude indicates the reference meridian.

The zero meridian passes through Greenwich (near London). The car's position is therefore defined as a parallel arc between the car's point and the reference meridian.

It is essential to indicate whether the longitude is East or West, the maximum value is 180°.

2 - Vehicle's speed in m/s along the south-north / east-west axes.

3 - PDOP of the GPS point (in actual fact an estimate of the variance on the GPS position error).

4 - Quality data relating to the signal received: (number of satellites, South/North relationship, point in 3D).

5 - Time-fix relating to the last measurement made (makes it possible to identify to which instant the measurement refers).

The system stops indicating residual range for values lower than 15 km (dashes are shown instead of the range value in km).

'instant consumption'

Indicates vehicle fuel consumption while driving and is therefore useful for showing fuel consumption for the driving style adopted. This value is the same as the two on-board computer functions ('From reset' and 'B da hh:mm').

The value is expressed as l/100 km: litres per 100 kilometres.

'average fuel consumption'

Indicates average fuel consumption measured since last refuelling.

The value is expressed as l/100 km: litres per 100 kilometres

'range'

Indicates the distance in kilometres the car still has to travel before it will need refuelling.

The calculated journey range depends on the amount of fuel still present in the tank and the average fuel consumption.

'average speed'

Indicates average car speed calculated from the last manual reset ('from reset' function) or automatic reset ('B da hh:mm' function) of on-board computer.

The value is expressed in 'km/h' (kilometres per hour).

'journey distance'

Indicates distance in kilometres travelled by the car since the last manual reset ('from reset' function) or automatic reset ('B da hh:mm' function) of on-board computer

The value is expressed in 'km' (kilometres).

'journey time'

Indicates time since the last manual reset ('from reset' function) or automatic reset ('B da hh:mm' function) of on-board computer.

The value is expressed in '(h) (m)' (hours and minutes).

'distance to destination'

This information, present only when the navigation function is active, indicates distance (in kilometres) between current car position and the set destination.

'arrival time'

This information, present only when the navigation function is active, indicates the estimated time at which the set destination will be reached. The time is indicated in 'hh:mm' (hours and minutes).

The indicated arrival time is obtained by increasing the remaining journey time by some 30%, calculated on the basis of average speed added to current time.

Introduction

Switching the system on/off and stand-by

Access to the system can be achieved in two different ways:

  • Automatic turning on with the ignition key in the ON position
  • Manual turning on by pressing the knob (R1)

Automatic turning on

When the ignition key is turned to the ON position the CONNECT system comes on automatically and all the functions described in this chapter are either activated or can be activated.

Manual turning on

When the ignition key is in the OFF position and the knob (R1) or the button (T22) is pressed, the CONNECT system comes on with all the following modules available:

  • MAIN
  • AUDIO
  • NAV
  • TEL

In this way the SETUP and TRIP modules can be activated, however, no parameter change or language change operation or any other type of adjustment can be validated. (These limitations are due to the fact that, with the vehicle switched off (key in OFF position), the internal date transmission devices are not working).

The system starts to work when the ignition key is in the ON position.

Turning the system off

There are two different ways of switching the CONNECT system off:

  • switching off independent of the ignition key
  • switching off dependent on the ignition key

To make this choice, access the SETUP menu.

When the first mode is activated the system can be switched off by pressing knob (R1).

When the second mode is activated the system can be switched off by turning the ignition key to the OFF position. With the engine running or the panel on, the system can be switched off by pressing knob (R1).

There is a 20 minute delay in switching the system off if there is a destination set or a telephone call is in progress.

Antitheft protection

The CONNECT is protected against theft and unauthorized systems by means of an 'authentication procedure'.

This type of check involves other devices installed on the vehicle including the Body Computer which uses messages exchanged via the telematic network and is activated each time the system is switched on.

The procedure is not activated if the CONNECT system is switched on using the knob (R1) or the button (T22) and if the ignition key is in the OFF position. In this case the CONNECT system works normally without carrying out the authentication procedure.

Entering the secret code

If the ignition is switched ON, the user is asked to enter the 4 digit Master Code to allow access to the standard functions.

The Master Code is unique to each CONNECT system and cannot be deleted.

To enter the code, a special screen must be accessed.

After having entered the code, a second screen indicates that the authetication procedure is in progress.

If the correct code has been provided the system is fully enabled; conversely, if an incorrect code has been entered, the screen is cancelled and the previous screen with the words 'The code entered is incorrect' appears. Enter the master code or switch the system off using the ON button.

There is no limit to the number of incorrect codes that can be entered.

The secret code has to be entered for the CONNECT to work after it has been connected to the vehicle's electrical system for the first time or to a different Body Computer from the original one or after a replacement of the system.

The can network

The TIN is a+15 node connected to the B-CAN network; this means that at Key OFF, the CONNECT is not connected to the network and cannot be reactivated by the network.

The Key On signal is in fact a direct signal to TIN.

The user can use the voice recognition function to control the CONNECT by voice in order to carry out certain phone functions.

Voice messages

This function allows the user to record and replay six voice messages, in order, with a total maximum duration of 30 seconds for each message. If the memory is full, the oldest message is overwritten. When the time available elapses, the operation ends automatically.

The recording activated by the user can last for a maximum of 30 seconds, and is terminated automatically at the end of this available time.

However, the user can interrupt it manually.

Both the beginning of the recording and the end (either terminated by the user or because the memory has run out), are identified by an appropriate acoustic message (double beep).

The Voice Memo allows you to listen to voice messages from the last message recorded and then all previous messages. Once the buffer is full, the messages are played again from the first (in a continuous loop).

The Voice Memo allows the entire buffer available for recording to be deleted.

Navigation system (nav)

General information

The navigation system in the CONNECT makes it possible to reach a pre-established destination by means of visual instructions and acoustic instructions. The navigation system is fast, convenient, safe and - above all - very flexible to use because it allows you to call up programmed destinations or reference points such as hotels, places of historical interest, public organisations, fuel stations or Alfa Romeo dealers.

The position of the vehicle is determined by means of the GPS (Global Positioning System) on board the vehicle. The GPS system is equipped with an aerial and a receiver module integrated in the telematic system. The system dynamically processes the satellite signals, the signals coming from the milometer, the reversing signal and the information from the gyroscope incorporated in the navigation calculator, integrating them with the current position of the vehicle to produce an 'estimated vehicle point'.

This estimated position tends to differ from the current position as a result of sensor imprecision. To correct this error, every 30 metres an algorithm is activated, called Map Matching, which correlates the journey made by the car with the road network present in the map data base.

The signals coming from the left and right milometers make it possible to determine the movement of the vehicle and whether it has turned off (identified by the difference travelled between the left and right wheels), whilst the reversing sensor identifies the direction of travel.

The Alfa Romeo navigation system helps the driver while driving and advises on the best route to the set destination by means of voice and graphic information.

The suggestions given by the navigation system do not release the driver from full responsability for manoeuvres carried out in traffic while driving the car and for respecting the highway code and other traffic regulations. The responsibility for road safety is always expected from the driver of the vehicle.

GPS reception is difficult under trees, between high buildings, in multi-storey car parks, in tunnels and anywhere where the satellite aerial reception could be obstructed.

If the battery has been disconnected fro the car, the GPS system takes about 15 minutes to become activated.

The GPS navigation system takes a few minutes to pinpoint the new car position after it has been turned off and the car driven without the system active (e.g. on a pick-up truck).

If there is no satellite information, the on board system uses information from the ABS sensors for an analysis of the data.

The GPS satellite aerial should not be covered by metal or damp objects.

This car's instantaneous position is identified in the navigation CD-ROM and shown on the display together with the topographical features of the area memorized on the CD. Access to the data on the CD-ROM requires a brief wait whilst the maps are displayed.

The system constantly compares the information coming from the milometer, from the reversing sensor, from the GPS aerial and from the gyroscope in order to automatically compensate for variations in temperature, pressure or any other eventuality which could affect the position reading in any way.

The precise autoadjustment of the navigation system requires 50/100 km to be covered after first activation and when the tyres are changed.

If the wheel grip conditions are poor (for example slipping on ice), the system will temporarily give an incorrect position reading.

During the autoadjustment the position reading is incomplete.

The navigation system is completely managed by the telecoms system therefore the only operations which may be necessary are replacing the CD-ROM with one with a map for another area or with an updated map.

Navigation cd-rom drive

The navigation system CD-ROM drive is located on the front of the telecoms system and is also used for the audio CD. It is not therefore possible to use the audio player and the navigation system drive simultaneously. The navigation system can, however, operate partially even without the navigation system CD-ROM inserted.

In this case, when the key is pressed to expel the CD-ROM with the navigation function activated (so an audio CD can be inserted), one of two things may happen:

  • the system cannot currently compute the required route;
  • the route computed before the navigation system CD-ROM was extracted is still valid.

In the first case, the car position alone will be displayed and you will be asked to insert the navigation system CD-ROM.

In the second case, the system is able to provide instructions to the destination and asks the user if the guide is to be maintained or not.

If the user selects and confirms NO, the system continues as in the first case. If YES is selected, the system stores the relevant part of the map; this operation takes a few instants and the display asks the user to wait.

When the CD-ROM is loaded, it is ejected and the system resumes the navigation system function with the maximum scale of '2 km'; in this case, not all the route may be visible.

Under these conditions, navigation is limited and and certain functions and commands will not be available. The information shown in the map will also be restricted.

When the navigation system is no longer able to continue guiding the driver to the destination, or the car leaves the portion of the map that has been loaded, the display asks the user to load the navigation system CD-ROM. If the user does not insert the CD-ROM the system operates as described in the first case above, i.e. suspending the map information and continuing using GPS information (car location and number of satellites available).

When the new CD-ROM is inserted, the system software will automatically be updated with the new maps or new functions. During the operation, a message will be displayed asking the user to wait and at the end the destination memory will be empty.

When the 'Infomobility' function is selected and confirmed using knob (R2), a message is sent to the service provider with an information request.

Some information will be sent directly by the operator while other information will be sent via SMS messages that are received regardless of which function is active (MAIN, AUDIO, etc.). The message appears directly above the screen active at the time, inside a window that contains functions 'Save', 'Delete', 'Map' and 'Call'.

If the 'Save' option is selected, the message will be stored, while if 'Delete' is selected, it will be eliminated from the display and from memory.

If 'Map' is selected, the point on the geographical map will be displayed automatically, with the possibility of inserting it as the destination of the navigation system. In this case the message will also be stored automatically.

If 'Call' is selected, the telephone number contained in the message will be dialled automatically and the message will be stored.

If a message sequence is received, a special window will be opened for each one and it will be possible to carryout the save, delete, display on map or call telephone number operations.

All message received will be saved unless they are deleted. The list with all the messages is visible at the bottom of the display, in the main screen of the 'Infomobility' function.

Each message is identified by an icon indicating type, date and time sent.

To access individual messages in the list, which may contain traffic information, points of interest or weather information, activate the 'Select' function using knob (R2), then turn to scroll through the list of messages (including the part that cannot be seen). When the message you want to read is highlighted, press knob (R2) to display on the screen.

An icon with a 'T' identifies messages with traffic information (e.g. accidents).

When the message contains geographical information to help locate the point, the options 'Delete' and 'Map' are made available when the display appears.

When 'Delete' is selected and confirmed, the message is removed from the list permanently, while 'Map' displays the map that shows the position of the point of interest from the event.

An icon with an 'i' identifies messages with information on points of interest or general information.

When the message is displayed, the 'Delete', 'Map' and 'Call' options are available.

When 'Delete' is selected and confirmed, the message is removed from the list permanently, while 'Map' displays a map that shows the position of the point of interest that may also be used as destination or inserted in the system list. With the 'Call' button, when present, a call can be sent directly to the number indicated in the message.

The icon with an 'i' also identifies messages with general information (weather conditions, atmospheric events, etc.).

When one of these messages, not accompanied by geographical information for location, is displayed, only the 'Delete' option is available, which allows it to be removed from the list permanently.

OPERATING PROBLEMS

The CONNECT system is capable of detecting and solving both any faults that are produced inside the system and any overheating problems

OPERATING FAULTS: if an internal fault relating to a certain module (audio, telephone, etc.) is identified, the system 'freezes' the last available screen and launches a diagnostic search. The system checks the module involved for a certain length of time to determine the type of fault; if the fault persists when this preset time is exceeded, the best action to solve the problem is implemented (e.g. resetting the hardware for the module involved).

If the system no longer responds to the commands, it can be restarted manually by pressing the TRIP button (T21) 4 times in the space of 3 seconds.

PROBLEMS DUE TO OVERHEATING: if the temperature of one of the system hardware modules (audio, telephone, CD player, etc) exceeds the maximum limit, the module will signal that it is overheated; a dedicated warning message will appear on the display.

The module concerned will be automatically restricted or disabled. In extreme cases the entire system is automatically shut down until the temperature returns to normal and this will be shown on the display, as illustrated in the diagram.

To exit the dialogue window, press the 'ESC' button; the module involved will operate on a restricted basis:

  • Overheating of the 'Audio' module: if the 'Audio' module overheats, the sound volume is automatically restricted irrespective of the audio source activated (radio, CD, CD Changer). A special warning message for the user will appear on the display.
  • Overheatin of the 'CD Player' module: if the 'CD Player' module overheats, no type of CD can be read: no audio CD can be listened to and the navigation functions cannot be guaranteed (unless the navigationsystem was activated previously without a CD). A warning message for the user will appear on the display.
  • Overheating of the 'Telephone' module: if the 'Telephone' module overheats, the module will be deactivated (TEL OFF) with the inhibitaion of the information and service functions (SOS). A special message for the user will appear on the display.
  • System auto-switching off; in the case of extreme overheating, a warning will notify the user that the system auto shut down procedure has begun. When normal temperature operating conditions are resumed, the user can switch the system back on again.
